text:
Aisha: Quick proposal — I want to try an "adaptive subpage coalesce" experiment to reduce fragmentation from lots of tiny KV-cache allocations. Goal: lower tail latency regressions caused by many tiny live fragments and reduce background compaction churn.

Aisha: High level: keep 64B subpage bitmap per arena; track free-run-lengths per region; when fragmentation + eviction pressure cross thresholds, coalesce adjacent free subpages into larger 2KB pages and move them into a compacted free pool. Coalesce only on background worker or on slow-path eviction to avoid adding jitter to allocations.

Ryan: Sketch looks promising. How does coalesce interact with offload/migration? If we merge subpages and then a shard gets migrated to host, we might blow up DMA scatter/gather or force additional host copies.

Aisha: Good call. Plan is to gate coalesce by residency pressure: only coalesce when host-residency % > X OR when node-wide eviction pressure > Y. We also keep a reversible map so coalesced pages can be split lazily on first touch to avoid mass migrations.

Maria: Can we avoid breaking any splitmap/pinned mapping invariants? If pinned subpage exists, coalesce must skip that region. Also need to preserve per-subpage pin counts.

Ben: Small practical note: we need an ABI change so callers can say AllocHint::allow_coalesce=false for latency-sensitive allocations (e.g., hot KV cache entries). Otherwise we risk regressing hot-paths.

Aisha: Agreed. Draft ABI snippet: 
```
enum AllocHints : u8 {
  NONE = 0,
  ALLOW_COALESCE = 1 << 0,
  PIN_ON_ALLOC = 1 << 1,
}
fn alloc(size, hints: AllocHints) -> ptr;
```
Background coalesce worker only touches allocations with ALLOW_COALESCE.

Ryan: Telemetry: we should emit histograms for "subpage.free_run_len", "coalesce.attempts", "coalesce.success_rate", and tag by tenant/model. Also capture tail-latency delta pre/post coalesce.

Aisha: Yep. My plan: add a lightweight sample every N seconds and an event when worker performs a coalesce sweep. We'll add canary dashboards.

deploy-bot: perf-test triggered: fragmentation-coalesce/experiment/2026-03-21-01 — status: queued :gear:

Jonas: Another concern: prefix KV cache semantics. If we coalesce and then drop/evict individual subpages later, ensure prefix lookup still works (we can't assume coalesced page always fully resident). Add unit tests for partial-split behavior.

Maria: +1 to canary on Dedicated first (predictable eviction patterns). Dedicated lets us tune thresholds without noisy multi-tenant effects.

Ben: Also think about compaction vs coalesce ordering. If compactor runs concurrently, we need fine-grained locking or epoch-based SWAP to avoid races. Prefer epoch tagging + CAS swap of arena metadata.

Aisha: I'll prototype with epoch tags + per-region lock striping. The lazy-split path will re-create subpage descriptors on-touch.

Ryan: When you push the RFC, include an experiment plan: workload mix (small-kv heavy, embed-cache), success criteria (25% less fragmented bytes, <1% tail latency impact), and rollback criteria.

Aisha: Will do. Posting a short checklist later. Thanks for the feedback all. :thumbsup:

Jonas: Also add a sanity check that coalesce doesn't increase total resident pages under low pressure (i.e., no accidental inflation).

Aisha: Good catch — will add guard: coalesce should never increase resident pages unless it's accompanied by a demote/evict pass.

Maria: LGTm for an RFC and a gated experiment.

Aisha: I'll open the PR and link the perf job here when started.
